key_insight: Replacing the static one-to-one connection between a single vision encoder output and the LLM with a trainable many-to-many cross-layer injection lets language models access hierarchical visual features on demand, enabling richer alignment of local details and global semantics for better multimodal reasoning.
problem_solved: Current VLM architectures bottleneck visual information by feeding only the final vision representation into the LLM, preventing effective use of multi-scale, hierarchical visual cues and limiting fine-grained grounding and compositional reasoning.
method: Introduce a dynamic cross-layer injection mechanism that connects multiple layers of the vision encoder to multiple layers of the LLM via learnable adapters or cross-attention blocks, enabling many-to-many information flow.
Use gating or routing to adaptively select and fuse visual features at different abstraction levels per LLM layer and per token, preserving local details and global context.
Train end-to-end with alignment objectives (e.g., multimodal contrastive, fusion-aware losses) so the model learns which visual layers to inject for different linguistic contexts and tasks.
impact: This design reduces the visual feature bottleneck and gives practitioners a scalable blueprint to build stronger, more interpretable vision-language systems that better integrate multi-scale perception with LLM reasoning across tasks like VQA, captioning, and multimodal instruction following.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: 'One-to-One' (single arrow from vision output to LLM input) vs 'Many-to-Many' (dense arrows between multiple vision and LLM layers) to show structural change.
Schematic of a cross-layer injection block showing adapters/cross-attention + gating/router and information flow per LLM token.
Attention / activation heatmaps illustrating how different visual layers contribute to different words or reasoning steps.
Bar or line chart summarizing qualitative gains (e.g., improved grounding or task robustness) and an ablation flow showing effect of dynamic routing vs static injection.
paper_title: From One-to-One to Many-to-Many: Dynamic Cross-Layer Injection for Deep Vision-Language Fusion
paper_authors: Cheng Chen, Yuyu Guo, Pengpeng Zeng, Jingkuan Song, Peng Di
